findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the cutover flag's production default (recommend default-OFF opt-in, enabled per-client after a canary), so rollout is staged rather than a single 100%-traffic flip.
evidence: 'the cutover is gated behind a single switch (config/flag) that restores the plain/identity path'
No stated default value for the switch
E6(f) not-applicable only 'when the cutover stays behind a non-default opt-in flag' — but default is unspecified
findings.finding: The cutover flag's DEFAULT state (on vs off in production) is never stated. The plan describes a rollback ('one revert') and a rollback test with 'the cutover flag off', but does not say whether the flag ships defaulting-on (a 100%-traffic behavior flip) or defaulting-off (opt-in). This is load-bearing for whether the cutover is a staged rollout or an all-traffic flip.
findings.location: Approach → 'Rollback' bullet; Scope → gated cutover; AC 'The cutover is flag-gated'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Rollback bullet: 'The cutover flag defaults OFF; it is enabled per-client (Cloud, then DC) after a canary tenant validates convergence, so no single flip touches all traffic.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the writer and write-point for the new inline `rich_sha` (e.g. folded into `_advance_baselines` at persist from `ctx.curr_snapshot`), and confirm it is a single writer that only touches the entry when the rendered wire changed.
evidence: 'store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] (8 bytes) inline in the binding'
'The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.'
'binding_store.py — inline change-gated rich_sha beside the existing baseline (_BASELINE_FIELDS).'
ABSENCE: no named function/step performs the rich_sha write, and the sole named writer (_advance_baselines) is described only as the baseline writer.
findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` state names its shape (8-byte sha256 of rendered wire), its change-gate discipline (no per-pass write), and that the compare is read-only, but it never names the WRITER: which function advances `rich_sha` and at what point in the pass. The plan is explicit that `_advance_baselines` is the single existing writer for the baseline and that the compare 'never writes back', which leaves the rich_sha write path unowned — is it a second writer, or is it folded into `_advance_baselines`?
findings.suggested_fix: State that `rich_sha` is advanced by the same single `_advance_baselines` writer at persist (change-gated on rendered-wire delta), so no second writer is introduced.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State precisely which push `rich_sha` suppresses that origin-gating (`local != baseline`) and the once-only re-emit compare do NOT already suppress (e.g. name the DC re-render-identical case and the read site that consults `rich_sha`), or drop `rich_sha` and gate re-render on the existing baseline/compare alone.
evidence: Plan: 'store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] (8 bytes) inline in the binding ... so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.'
Plan already asserts origin-gating suffices to suppress: 'a description update fires only when local differs from baseline (a rebar-side edit)'
Plan already asserts once-only convergence: 'an already-synced body re-emits exactly once ... then converges (the existing once-only re-emit mechanism)'

Codebase: outbound_field_diff.py:273-293 (fit + compare vs canonical_remote) and _suppressed_by_inbound:248 (local-vs-baseline) already provide the emit gate; binding_store.py:105 _BASELINE_FIELDS is the existing per-binding state — rich_sha adds a new field beside it
ABSENCE: no plan sentence describes reading rich_sha to skip an emit; it is only 'stored' and declared comparison-only
findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` per-binding state is a third emission gate whose necessity is not established by the plan's own logic: the plan already describes outbound description emit as fully gated by origin-gating (`local != baseline`) AND the once-only re-emit compare (`fitted != canonical_remote`), and states the compare 'stays comparison-only and never writes back' — but never names a read/consume site where `rich_sha` gates a push. The plan justifies rich_sha's SIZING (0.07 KB/version vs the rejected per-pass timestamp) but not what re-push it prevents that the existing baseline-diff + emit-compare do not.
findings.location: Plan §'Origin-gating so Jira-native constructs survive (AC5)'; §Scope (binding_store.py bullet); AC 'The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte rich_sha'
scenarios: No-op pass (local == baseline): origin-gating already emits nothing, so rich_sha adds no observable suppression.
Rebar-originated edit (local != baseline): the emit-compare already decides re-push; unclear what rich_sha changes.

DC path re-renders every pass via normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(...)) at outbound_mapper.py:77 — if THIS is the motivation (skip pushing an identical re-render), the plan does not connect rich_sha to it as the consuming gate.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the second DC CREATE-path description codec site `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC` (adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:40, applied at :111 in `_translate_create_fields`) and state/verify that re-applying `fit_outbound` to the already-rendered wiki from backend.py:70 is idempotent and does not un-render or double-transform the body.
evidence: Plan: 'The DC CREATE path is a SEPARATE, explicitly-enumerated codec consumer: `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (backend.py:70) constructs its OWN WikiTextCodec() and builds "description": codec.fit_outbound(...)'
adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:40 `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()`; :111 `fields["description"] = _DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)` inside _translate_create_fields (:93)
backend.py:93 `_DCOutbound.map_local_to_remote` returns `_map_local_to_dc_fields(ticket)`; that payload feeds create_issue (_issues.py:139/162) -> _translate_create_fields
The plan claims create rendering is achieved by 'compose the renderer/to_wire with fit_outbound' at backend.py:70 only, with no mention of the _issues.py:111 re-fit
findings.finding: The DC CREATE path applies the description codec at TWO sites, but the plan enumerates only one. The create payload built by _map_local_to_dc_fields (backend.py:70, the plan's named site) flows through create_issue into _translate_create_fields (adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:93), which at _issues.py:109-111 re-applies a SEPARATE module-level `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()` (_issues.py:40) via `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)`. The plan changes WikiTextCodec and renders at backend.py:70 but never enumerates this second create-path codec consumer, so it is unclear whether the already-rendered wiki is re-fit harmlessly or (e.g. via a future format-aware fit) un-rendered/double-transformed.
findings.location: Plan sections 'The live cutover (both clients)' / 'Scope' — DC CREATE-path bullet naming only adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:70
scenarios: A new DC issue is created after cutover: backend.py:70 renders wiki, then _translate_create_fields re-fits the rendered wiki at _issues.py:111
A future format-aware change to WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound (the docstring at backend.py:140-143 anticipates one) alters the rendered create body at the unenumerated site
findings.suggested_fix: Add _issues.py:40/111 to the DC CREATE-path scope and add an assertion (or note) that fit_outbound on already-rendered wiki is an idempotent no-op, so the create body stays rendered; the `test_dc_cutover_converges` create case should exercise the full backend.py:70 -> create_issue -> _translate_create_fields chain.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the transport-level DC create writer `_translate_create_fields`/`_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound` (`_issues.py:40`,`:93`,`:111`) to the DC CREATE-path codec-consumer inventory (derived from the `WikiTextCodec` reference graph, not hand-picked), and specify whether it renders (compose renderer before fit) or is proven idempotent under render-then-fit, plus update its pin tests (test_dc_create_field_translation_18a5.py, test_dc_backend_characterization.py).
evidence: Plan: 'The DC CREATE path is a SEPARATE, explicitly-enumerated codec consumer: `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (`backend.py:70`) constructs its OWN `WikiTextCodec()` ... applying only `fit_outbound`, never `to_wire` ... This story changes `_map_local_to_dc_fields` to render before the fit'

src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:40 `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()`; :111 `fields["description"] = _DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)`; :162 `fields = _translate_create_fields(ticket_data)`; :164 `self._client.create_issue(**fields)`

grep for `WikiTextCodec` surfaces the `_issues.py:40`/`:24` create-path instance the plan omits; grep for `fit_outbound` confirms `_issues.py:111` as a distinct description-fit site from `backend.py:70`
findings.finding: The DC CREATE-path codec-consumer inventory names only `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (backend.py:70), but a second independent `WikiTextCodec()` description-fit consumer on the create path — `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC` (`_issues.py:40`) invoked as `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)` inside `_translate_create_fields` (`_issues.py:93`/`:111`), the transport writer actually reaching `client.create_issue(**fields)` from `create_issue` (`_issues.py:139`/`:162`) — is not enumerated. Like `_map_local_to_dc_fields` it applies only `fit_outbound`, never `to_wire`, so by the plan's own rationale it does not render; changing only `_map_local_to_dc_fields` leaves this site un-updated. The inventory reads as hand-picked (single named site) rather than derived from the WikiTextCodec reference graph, which surfaces this second create-path instance.
findings.location: The live cutover → DC: 'The DC CREATE path is a SEPARATE, explicitly-enumerated codec consumer: `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (backend.py:70) ... changes `_map_local_to_dc_fields` to render before the fit'; Scope: 'adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py (:70) — DC CREATE-path'
scenarios: _issues.py:111 `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)` re-fits the create payload's description at the transport layer; if it receives raw Markdown it never renders and a newly-created DC issue still ships plain Markdown despite the plan claiming create ships rendered wiki (AC: test_dc_cutover_converges create leg would regress).

If it receives the already-rendered value from a fixed `_map_local_to_dc_fields`, `fit_outbound` re-runs on rendered wiki; the plan neither routes it through the renderer nor proves render-then-fit is idempotent, so a truncation or double-fit hazard is unmodeled.

The DC create-path double-fit is pinned by test_dc_create_field_translation_18a5.py (`test_the_description_survives_the_translation`, :285) and test_dc_backend_characterization.py; those pins target `_translate_create_fields`/`WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` and would need updating alongside the cutover but are not in the test inventory.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a staged rollout (canary tenant / subset of bindings) for enabling the cutover flag before full per-client enablement.
evidence: 'a bad rollout is one revert, not a code rewrite' — describes rollback but not staged rollout

findings.finding: The plan does not describe a staged/canary rollout for the wire-format change — only an all-or-nothing per-client flag plus a revert path. A codec cutover that changes what every synced description ships to Jira is a runtime behavior change to a long-running reconciler, but no canary tenant / progressive enablement is specified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the DC codec's behavior when render_markdown_to_wiki fails (plain-text fallback + surfaced error/metric), matching the Cloud whole-codec fallback.
evidence: Cloud bullet: 'install the whole-codec plain-text fallback'
DC bullet has no equivalent fallback clause — only 'delegates to wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki'
T5b(a): error states surfaced, not swallowed; graceful-degradation present
findings.finding: A DC codec rendering-failure fallback is not specified. The plan installs 'the whole-codec plain-text fallback' for Cloud only; for DC it merely redefines to_wire→render_markdown_to_wiki and normalize_outbound. If render_markdown_to_wiki raises on malformed Markdown, the outbound send path and the baseline compare have no stated degraded/graceful path.
findings.location: 'The live cutover' → DC bullet; Scope → rich_text.py
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the DC cutover bullet: 'WikiTextCodec wraps render_markdown_to_wiki in a try/except that falls back to the plain string on render failure and emits a metric/log, mirroring the Cloud whole-codec fallback.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the cutover convergence ACs exercise the actual live send boundary (acli encode call / DC `issue.update`) end-to-end, or if that is stubbed, document why the substitute faithfully represents the production wire payload.
evidence: 'repoint the four AdfCodec ops ... reroute the live consumers ... the encode at adapters/jira/acli.py:205 and acli_cli_ops.py:369'
'this redefinition is exactly what makes issue.update(fields=…) begin shipping rendered wiki — the cutover'
'After the DC cutover, issue.update(fields=…) receives rendered wiki (not raw Markdown)'
ABSENCE: no AC specifies the send is exercised against the real acli/issue.update boundary rather than an offline stub of it.
findings.finding: This is a CUTOVER that makes a new rich-codec path the DEFAULT live send (Cloud acli/acli_cli_ops encode, DC issue.update). The convergence ACs assert 'posts once' and 'issue.update(fields=…) receives rendered wiki', but the plan does not state whether the live send boundary (the acli command / DC `issue.update`) is exercised end-to-end or asserted only against an offline/mock substitute. If the ACs are satisfiable purely by offline codec-composition assertions that stub the real send, the suite can go green while the defaulted live wire path is broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC asserting the defaulted send path is exercised against the real (or captured-at-boundary) acli/issue.update payload so the rendered wire is proven to leave the client, not just that the codec composes correctly in-process.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the title's 'LWW' term with the body's settled local-wins policy (rename the title to 'local-wins conflict safety' or note LWW is realized as local-wins).
